title: The Uncanny Valley: Why Almost-Human Things Disturb Us
question: Why do robots, animated faces, and lifelike prosthetics that look almost—but not quite—human provoke revulsion, when things that look distinctly non-human or perfectly human do not?
summary: Our comfort with human likeness rises steadily with realism, then plunges sharply just before it reaches true human perfection, and climbs back up only once the illusion is complete. That dip — the uncanny valley — turns out to be less about how human something looks and more about the discomfort of not knowing which category it belongs to.
